fullPassage:
Astronaut Yujin's Space Log

Day 1 Back to Space!
After blasting off from Earth, we took about 27 hours to reach the International Space Station, where we docked successfully. This is my third journey into space. After ten years, I'm back on this station, the largest artificial space habitat in orbit 400 kilometers away from Earth!

Day 5 The World with No Gravity
Now I'm getting better at remembering where I am when I first wake up, but I'm still often confused about how my body is positioned. In the dark and without gravity, my inner ear just takes a random guess as to my position, and sometimes I wake up convinced that I'm upside down. Of course, it's actually my brain readjusting to an environment where height and weight lose their meaning. I can use any wall equally as if each were a floor. Everything has zero weight. This enables me not only to fly but also to lift huge objects with one finger as if I were a superhero. Unfortunately, zero gravity also makes astronauts lose muscle and bone density really fast. That's why I exercise for 150 minutes a day as my colleagues do.

Day 25 Starting the Day
The station orbits Earth once every 90 minutes, and the sun rises and sets every 45 minutes. However, our schedules are set to Greenwich Mean Time on Earth.

My day starts around 6:00 a.m. in my personal space, which is about the size of a phone booth. Still in my sleeping bag, I click through new emails and brush my teeth. I swallow the toothpaste with a sip of water from a bag with a straw. There's no good way to spit in space because everything floats. Then, I look over the daily schedule sent by the flight control team on Earth. After a meeting with the Earth team at 7:30, I start work.

Every minute of an astronaut's day is planned by the Earth team. My work comprises lots of scientific experiments and maintenance of the station. My favorite experiment is growing basil from seeds as I film its growth every day. Having green plants in space is a delight!

Day 60 Spacewalk!
Today's mission required a spacewalk, one of the riskiest tasks on the ISS. We had to install the bases for some newly developed solar batteries on the outside of the station.

Scott, my colleague, and I went to an airlock, a room connected to the outside of the station, put on our spacesuits, and floated gently into space. The large blue dome of Earth hovered overhead, looking like it was ready to come crashing down upon us. Forcing myself to focus on the task, I secured the hook of my safety cable to a ring just outside the airlock. We moved along the handrail to the edge of the station. The dark void in front of us seemed endless. Despite the safety cable, panic rose in me. I thought, "If my hand misses the handrail, I will fall into the void." The task seemed to take forever, but I finally managed to install the battery bases. When I turned my head, the bright blue Earth was still there. In the middle of darkness, its beauty was beyond description.

Day 99 One Day Left
I'll return to Earth tomorrow. If getting up into space is alarming and uncomfortable, coming back down is one of the most dangerous and physically harsh things an astronaut ever does. Back on Earth, I'll miss lots of things here. I'll miss the satisfaction of successfully finishing an experiment or a challenging task like a spacewalk. I'll especially miss my basil plants, whose leaves have become a dense forest! All the same, I'll never forget how lucky we are to have that wonderful blue planet as our home.

Day 100 The Descent to Earth
Mother Earth didn't exactly welcome us back with open arms. Earth's atmosphere is resistant to objects entering from space. Any object will create enough friction simply to burn up from the heat. This protects the planet from the orbital debris that would otherwise rain down on it. But it also meant we had to survive a fall through the atmosphere that created temperatures up to 1650 degrees Celsius.

After pushing our spaceship away from the station, we eased our way into the upper layers of the atmosphere to start our descent. We felt gravity begin to return. My watch felt a lot heavier on my wrist, and breathing got harder. The capsule heated up, and orange and purple flaming pieces flew by the window, which was scorched black. We were falling faster than the speed of sound. Once we got into the atmosphere about eight kilometers above the planet, a parachute caught us with a sudden halt and dragged and swung our capsule wildly through the sky until we hit the ground.

It's hard to describe how heavy everything felt in those first few minutes after landing. My arms felt terribly heavy, and so did my legs. Getting used to gravity, which I missed in space, will take quite a long time. The important thing is I'm home. I can smell the grass and feel the wind and the rain! I'll remember how magical these things are for the rest of my life.

questions.passage: I'll return to Earth tomorrow. If getting up into space is (A)[alarming / soothing] and uncomfortable, coming back down is one of the most dangerous and physically harsh things an astronaut ever does. Back on Earth, I'll miss lots of things here. I'll miss the satisfaction of successfully finishing an experiment or a (B)[challenging / effortless] task like a spacewalk. I'll especially miss my basil plants, whose leaves have become a (C)[dense / scattered] forest!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 우주로 올라가는 것은 경각심을 주는(alarming) 일이고, 우주유영 같은 어려운(challenging) 임무, 바질 잎이 빽빽한(dense) 숲이 되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① alarming(경각심을 주는) — challenging(도전적인) — dense(빽빽한): 원문과 일치 ←정답
❌ ② soothing(진정시키는) — challenging — dense: soothing은 alarming의 반의어로 문맥에 맞지 않음
❌ ③ alarming — effortless(수월한) — scattered(흩어진): effortless는 challenging의 반의어, scattered는 dense의 반의어
❌ ④ soothing — effortless — dense: A와 B 모두 원문과 반대
det.tip: alarming(불안한) ↔ soothing(안심되는). challenging(어려운) ↔ effortless(힘 안 드는). dense(밀집한) ↔ scattered(흩어진).

questions.passage: Mother Earth didn't exactly welcome us back with open arms. Earth's atmosphere is (A)[resistant / receptive] to objects entering from space. Any object will create enough friction simply to burn up from the heat. This protects the planet from the (B)[orbital / terrestrial] debris that would otherwise rain down on it. But it also meant we had to survive a fall through the atmosphere that created (C)[temperatures / pressures] up to 1650 degrees Celsius.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 지구 대기는 우주에서 들어오는 물체에 저항하는(resistant), 궤도의(orbital) 잔해, 섭씨 1650도의 온도(temperatures).
det.analysis:
❌ ① receptive(수용적인) — orbital — temperatures: receptive는 resistant의 반의어, 대기가 물체를 '수용'한다면 보호 기능과 모순
❌ ② resistant — terrestrial(지상의) — temperatures: terrestrial은 '지상의'란 뜻으로, 우주 잔해를 설명하는 orbital이 적절
✅ ③ resistant(저항하는) — orbital(궤도의) — temperatures(온도): 원문과 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ resistant — orbital — pressures(압력): 섭씨 1650도는 온도 단위이므로 pressures는 부적절
det.tip: resistant(저항하는) ↔ receptive(수용적인). orbital(궤도의) ↔ terrestrial(지상의). degrees Celsius는 온도(temperature) 단위.

questions.passage: Scott, my colleague, and I went to an airlock, a room connected to the outside of the station, put on our spacesuits, and floated (A)[gently / abruptly] into space. The large blue dome of Earth hovered overhead, looking like it was ready to come crashing down upon us. Forcing myself to focus on the task, I (B)[secured / loosened] the hook of my safety cable to a ring just outside the airlock. We moved along the handrail to the edge of the station. The dark void in front of us seemed (C)[endless / bounded].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 우주복을 입고 부드럽게(gently) 우주로 나갔고, 안전 케이블 고리를 고정했으며(secured), 어두운 허공이 끝없이(endless) 펼쳐져 보였다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① abruptly(갑자기) — secured — endless: abruptly는 우주유영 시 부드럽게 떠다니는 상황과 모순
✅ ② gently(부드럽게) — secured(고정한) — endless(끝없는): 원문과 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ gently — loosened(풀어놓은) — bounded(한정된): loosened는 안전 장비를 '풀다'로 위험한 행위, bounded는 끝없는 허공 묘사와 모순
❌ ④ abruptly — loosened — endless: A와 B 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: gently(부드럽게) ↔ abruptly(갑자기). secured(고정하다) ↔ loosened(풀다). endless(끝없는) ↔ bounded(한정된).

questions.passage: Now I'm getting better at remembering where I am when I first wake up, but I'm still often ①<u>confused</u> about how my body is positioned. In the dark and without gravity, my inner ear just takes a random guess as to my position, and sometimes I wake up convinced that I'm upside down. Of course, it's actually my brain ②<u>readjusting</u> to an environment where height and weight lose their meaning. I can use any wall equally as if each were a floor. Everything has zero weight. This enables me not only to fly but also to lift huge objects with one finger as if I were a superhero. Unfortunately, zero gravity also makes astronauts ③<u>gain</u> muscle and bone density really fast. That's why I ④<u>exercise</u> for 150 minutes a day as my colleagues do.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ gain(얻다) → lose(잃다): 무중력 상태에서는 근육과 골밀도를 잃는다. 운동을 150분이나 하는 이유.
det.analysis:
✅ ① confused(혼란스러운): 몸의 위치를 모르겠다는 문맥에 적절 — 원문 일치
✅ ② readjusting(재적응하는): 뇌가 환경에 다시 적응하는 것 — 원문 일치
❌ ③ gain(얻다) → lose(잃다): 무중력이 근육과 골밀도를 '얻게' 한다면 운동이 필요 없음. 원문은 lose ←정답
✅ ④ exercise(운동하다): 골밀도 감소를 막기 위해 운동한다 — 원문 일치
det.tip: lose muscle/bone density(근육/골밀도 감소) ↔ gain(증가). 무중력에서 신체가 약해지므로 매일 150분 운동.

questions.passage: After pushing our spaceship away from the station, we eased our way into the upper layers of the atmosphere to start our descent. We felt gravity begin to return. My watch felt a lot ①<u>heavier</u> on my wrist, and breathing got ②<u>easier</u>. The capsule heated up, and orange and purple flaming pieces flew by the window, which was ③<u>scorched</u> black. We were falling faster than the speed of ④<u>sound</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② easier(더 쉬운) → harder(더 어려운): 중력이 돌아오면서 호흡이 '쉬워진' 것이 아니라 '어려워진' 것.
det.analysis:
✅ ① heavier(더 무거운): 중력이 돌아오며 시계가 무겁게 느껴짐 — 원문 일치
❌ ② easier(더 쉬운) → harder(더 어려운): 대기 재진입 시 중력 증가로 호흡이 힘들어짐 ←정답
✅ ③ scorched(그을린): 창문이 검게 그을림 — 원문 일치
✅ ④ sound(소리): 음속보다 빠르게 떨어졌다 — 원문 일치
det.tip: harder(더 어려운) ↔ easier(더 쉬운). 중력이 돌아오면 몸이 무거워지고 호흡이 힘들어진다.

questions.passage:
My day starts around 6:00 a.m. in my personal space, which is about the size of a phone booth. Still in my sleeping bag, I click through new emails and brush my teeth. I swallow the toothpaste with a sip of water from a bag with a straw. There's no good way to spit in space because everything ①<u>floats</u>. Then, I look over the daily schedule sent by the flight control team on Earth. After a meeting with the Earth team at 7:30, I start work.

Every minute of an astronaut's day is ②<u>planned</u> by the Earth team. My work comprises lots of scientific experiments and ③<u>maintenance</u> of the station. My favorite experiment is growing basil from seeds as I film its growth every day. Having green plants in space is a ④<u>burden</u>!
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ burden(부담) → delight(기쁨): 가장 좋아하는 실험인 바질 재배를 언급하며 우주에서 초록 식물이 있다는 것이 '부담'이 아니라 '기쁨'.
det.analysis:
✅ ① floats(떠다닌다): 무중력에서 모든 것이 떠다니므로 침을 뱉을 수 없다 — 원문 일치
✅ ② planned(계획된다): 우주비행사의 하루는 지구 팀이 계획한다 — 원문 일치
✅ ③ maintenance(유지보수): 정거장의 과학 실험과 유지보수 — 원문 일치
❌ ④ burden(부담) → delight(기쁨): '가장 좋아하는 실험'이라는 앞 문맥과 모순 ←정답
det.tip: delight(기쁨) ↔ burden(부담). favorite experiment라는 문맥이 핵심 단서.

questions.passage: It's hard to describe how heavy everything felt in those first few minutes after landing. My arms felt terribly heavy, and so did my legs. Getting used to __________, which I missed in space, will take quite a long time. The important thing is I'm home. I can smell the grass and feel the wind and the rain! I'll remember how magical these things are for the rest of my life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 우주에서 그리워했던 중력(gravity)에 다시 적응하는 데 시간이 걸린다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① friction(마찰): 대기 마찰은 하강 시 언급되지만 이 문맥에서는 부적절
✅ ② gravity(중력): 우주에서 그리워했고, 무거움을 느끼는 원인 — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ density(밀도): 골밀도 관련 용어이지만 '그리워했다'와 맞지 않음
❌ ④ atmosphere(대기): 대기에 '적응'한다는 표현은 자연스럽지 않음
det.tip: gravity(중력)는 이 글의 핵심 주제. 우주에서는 없었고 지구로 돌아오면 다시 느끼는 힘.

questions.passage: Mother Earth didn't exactly welcome us back with open arms. Earth's atmosphere is resistant to objects entering from space. Any object will create enough __________ simply to burn up from the heat. This protects the planet from the orbital debris that would otherwise rain down on it. But it also meant we had to survive a fall through the atmosphere that created temperatures up to 1650 degrees Celsius.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 물체가 타버릴 만큼의 마찰(friction)을 발생시킨다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① gravity(중력): 중력은 물체를 끌어당기지만 '열로 타버리게' 하는 원인은 아님
❌ ② pressure(압력): 압력은 열을 직접 발생시키는 원인으로 설명하기 부적절
❌ ③ density(밀도): 밀도는 물질의 성질이지 '열로 타버리게' 하는 힘이 아님
✅ ④ friction(마찰): 대기 진입 시 마찰이 열을 발생시켜 물체가 타버림 ←정답
det.tip: friction(마찰)은 대기 재진입 시 열을 발생시키는 핵심 원인. burn up from the heat이 결정적 단서.

questions.passage:
The station orbits Earth once every 90 minutes, and the sun rises and sets every 45 minutes. However, our schedules are set to Greenwich Mean Time on Earth.

My day starts around 6:00 a.m. in my personal space, which is about the size of a phone booth. Still in my sleeping bag, I click through new emails and brush my teeth. I swallow the toothpaste with a sip of water from a bag with a straw. There's no good way to spit in space because everything __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 우주에서 침을 뱉을 방법이 없는 이유는 모든 것이 떠다니기(floats) 때문이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① floats(떠다닌다): 무중력에서 모든 것이 떠다니므로 침을 뱉으면 떠다님 — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② sinks(가라앉다): 무중력에서는 가라앉지 않음, 문맥 반대
❌ ③ melts(녹다): 온도와 관련된 변화이지 무중력과 무관
❌ ④ evaporates(증발하다): 상태 변화이지 무중력의 효과가 아님
det.tip: floats(떠다니다)는 무중력의 핵심 특징. 우주에서는 액체도 공중에 떠다닌다.

questions.passage: Today's mission required a spacewalk, one of the <u>riskiest</u> tasks on the ISS. We had to install the bases for some newly developed solar batteries on the outside of the station. Scott, my colleague, and I went to an airlock, a room connected to the outside of the station, put on our spacesuits, and floated gently into space. The large blue dome of Earth hovered overhead, looking like it was ready to come crashing down upon us.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 riskiest와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: riskiest(가장 위험한) = most dangerous(가장 위험한).
det.analysis:
❌ ① safest(가장 안전한): riskiest의 반의어로 정반대
❌ ② simplest(가장 단순한): 난이도를 나타내며 위험도와 무관
✅ ③ most dangerous(가장 위험한): risky와 dangerous는 '위험한'이라는 동의어 ←정답
❌ ④ most exciting(가장 흥미진진한): 자극적이라는 뜻이지 위험과는 다른 의미
det.tip: risky = dangerous = hazardous = perilous (위험한). 동의어 계열을 함께 외우기.

questions.passage: My work comprises lots of scientific experiments and maintenance of the station. My favorite experiment is growing basil from seeds as I film its growth every day. Having green plants in space is a <u>delight</u>! Today's mission required a spacewalk, one of the riskiest tasks on the ISS. We had to install the bases for some newly developed solar batteries on the outside of the station.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 delight와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: delight(기쁨) = pleasure(즐거움). 우주에서 초록 식물을 기르는 것이 기쁨이라는 문맥.
det.analysis:
❌ ① burden(부담): delight의 반의어에 가까움, 즐거움과 정반대
❌ ② challenge(도전): 어려움을 뜻하며 기쁨과는 다른 의미
❌ ③ routine(일상): 반복적인 일과라는 뜻으로 감정과 무관
✅ ④ pleasure(즐거움): delight와 '기쁨, 즐거움'으로 동의어 ←정답
det.tip: delight = pleasure = joy = happiness (기쁨, 즐거움).

questions.passage: After pushing our spaceship away from the station, we eased our way into the upper layers of the atmosphere to start our <u>descent</u>. We felt gravity begin to return. My watch felt a lot heavier on my wrist, and breathing got harder. The capsule heated up, and orange and purple flaming pieces flew by the window, which was scorched black.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 descent와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: descent(하강) = drop(하강). 우주선이 대기로 내려가기 시작하는 상황.
det.analysis:
❌ ① ascent(상승): descent의 정반대, 올라가는 것
✅ ② drop(하강): descent와 '아래로 내려가다'라는 동의어 ←정답
❌ ③ orbit(궤도): 궤도를 도는 것이지 하강이 아님
❌ ④ launch(발사): 우주로 쏘아 올리는 것으로 descent와 반대 방향
det.tip: descent(하강) = drop = fall. ↔ ascent(상승) = rise.

questions.passage: After blasting off from Earth, we took about 27 hours to reach the International Space Station, where we docked successfully. This is my third journey into space. After ten years, I'm back on this station, the largest <u>artificial</u> space habitat in orbit 400 kilometers away from Earth!
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 artificial과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: artificial(인공의) ↔ natural(자연의).
det.analysis:
✅ ① natural(자연의): artificial(인공의)의 정반대 ←정답
❌ ② complex(복잡한): 구조의 복잡성을 나타내며 인공/자연 축과 무관
❌ ③ orbital(궤도의): 위치를 나타내는 형용사로 반의어가 아님
❌ ④ permanent(영구적인): 시간적 지속성을 나타내며 다른 의미 축
det.tip: artificial(인공의) ↔ natural(자연의). 인간이 만든 것 vs 자연에 존재하는 것.

questions.passage: Earth's atmosphere is <u>resistant</u> to objects entering from space. Any object will create enough friction simply to burn up from the heat. This protects the planet from the orbital debris that would otherwise rain down on it. But it also meant we had to survive a fall through the atmosphere that created temperatures up to 1650 degrees Celsius.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 resistant와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: resistant(저항하는) ↔ vulnerable(취약한). 대기가 외부 물체에 '저항'하는 것과 반대로 '취약'하다면 보호 기능이 없는 것.
det.analysis:
❌ ① hostile(적대적인): 저항과 비슷한 느낌이지만 '공격적'이라는 뉘앙스로 반의어 아님, 다른 의미 축
❌ ② durable(내구성 있는): 오래 견디는 성질로 resistant와 유사한 방향
✅ ③ vulnerable(취약한): resistant의 반의어, 저항력이 없어 쉽게 영향받는 상태 ←정답
❌ ④ rigid(단단한): 물리적 강도를 나타내며 저항의 반대가 아님
det.tip: resistant(저항하는/내성 있는) ↔ vulnerable(취약한/무방비의). susceptible도 반의어.

questions.passage:
(A) The station <u>orbits</u> Earth once every 90 minutes, and the sun rises and sets every 45 minutes.

(B) After ten years, I'm back on this station, the largest artificial space habitat in <u>orbit</u> 400 kilometers away from Earth!
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)의 orbits와 (B)의 orbit의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 정거장이 지구를 90분마다 한 바퀴 돈다(orbits, 동사). (B) 지구에서 400km 떨어진 궤도(orbit, 명사)에 있는 거주지.
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 궤도(명사) — (B) 돌다(동사): A와 B의 품사가 뒤바뀜, 주어+동사 구조에서 orbits는 동사
❌ ② (A) 감시하다 — (B) 궤도: orbit에 '감시하다'라는 의미는 없음
❌ ③ (A) 돌다 — (B) 영역: orbit의 명사 의미는 '궤도'이지 '영역'이 아님
✅ ④ (A) 돌다(동사) — (B) 궤도(명사): 각각의 문맥에서 동사/명사로 올바르게 해석 ←정답
det.tip: orbit: ① (동사) ~의 궤도를 돌다 ② (명사) 궤도, 궤도 비행. 같은 단어가 품사에 따라 의미가 달라진다.

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어를 고르시오.

"the work needed to keep something in good condition"

det.korean: "무언가를 좋은 상태로 유지하기 위해 필요한 작업" → maintenance(유지보수).
det.analysis:
❌ ① experiment(실험): 새로운 것을 시험하는 것이지 유지하는 것이 아님
❌ ② habitat(거주지): 살아가는 공간을 뜻하며 유지 작업과 무관
✅ ③ maintenance(유지보수): '좋은 상태를 유지하기 위한 작업'과 정확히 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ descent(하강): 아래로 내려가는 행위를 뜻함
det.tip: maintenance(유지보수): maintain(유지하다)의 명사형. 본문에서 station의 maintenance가 언급됨.

questions.passage: I'll miss the __________ (satisfy) of successfully finishing an experiment or a challenging task like a spacewalk.

overlay.excerptSentences: I'll miss the __________ (satisfy) of successfully finishing an experiment or a challenging task like a spacewalk.

questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: the __________ of 구조에서 관사(the) 뒤에 명사가 필요하므로 satisfy(동사) → satisfaction(명사, 만족감).
det.analysis: ✅ satisfaction: satisfy(동사, 만족시키다) → satisfaction(명사, 만족감). the + 명사 + of 구조에서 명사 필요.
det.tip: satisfy(동사) → satisfaction(명사) → satisfying(형용사, 만족스러운) → satisfied(형용사, 만족한).

questions.passage: This protects the planet from the __________ (orbit) debris that would otherwise rain down on it.

overlay.excerptSentences: This protects the planet from the __________ (orbit) debris that would otherwise rain down on it.

questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: the __________ debris에서 명사(debris)를 수식하는 형용사가 필요하므로 orbit(명사) → orbital(형용사, 궤도의).
det.analysis: ✅ orbital: orbit(명사, 궤도) → orbital(형용사, 궤도의). debris를 수식하는 형용사 자리.
det.tip: orbit(명사, 궤도) → orbital(형용사, 궤도의). -al 접미사가 형용사를 만든다.

questions.passage: The dark void in front of us seemed endless. Despite the safety cable, panic rose in me. I thought, "If my hand misses the handrail, I will fall into the void." The task seemed to take forever, but I finally managed to install the battery bases. When I turned my head, the bright blue Earth was still there. In the middle of darkness, its beauty was __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 어둠 속에서 지구의 아름다움은 말로 표현할 수 없었다(beyond description).
det.analysis:
❌ ① hard to ignore(무시하기 어려운): 의미는 통하지만 원문 표현이 아님, 감탄의 깊이가 부족
✅ ② beyond description(형용할 수 없는): 원문과 일치, 아름다움이 말로 표현할 수 없다는 관용구 ←정답
❌ ③ within expectation(예상 범위 내의): 아름다움에 놀란 문맥과 정반대
❌ ④ under examination(조사 중인): 과학적 맥락이지만 아름다움을 묘사하는 데 부적절
det.tip: beyond description = 형용할 수 없는. beyond + 명사 = ~를 넘어선.

questions.passage: In the dark and without gravity, my inner ear just takes a random guess as to my position, and sometimes I wake up convinced that I'm upside down. Of course, it's actually my brain readjusting to an environment where height and weight lose their meaning. I can use any wall equally as if each were a floor. Everything has zero weight. This enables me not only to fly but also to lift huge objects with one finger __________.

overlay.blank: as if I were a superhero

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: as long as I stay focused
as if I were a superhero

det.korean: 손가락 하나로 거대한 물체를 들어올릴 수 있는 것이 마치 슈퍼히어로인 것처럼(as if I were a superhero).
det.analysis:
❌ ① without any difficulty(어려움 없이): 의미는 비슷하지만 비유적 표현이 아닌 직설적 표현, 원문의 생생한 비유를 담지 못함
❌ ② despite the heavy weight(무거운 무게에도 불구하고): zero weight라고 했으므로 heavy weight는 모순
❌ ③ as long as I stay focused(집중하는 한): 무중력의 능력과 집중력은 관계없음, 조건이 필요 없는 상황
✅ ④ as if I were a superhero(마치 슈퍼히어로인 것처럼): 원문과 일치, 가정법 비유 표현 ←정답
det.tip: as if + 가정법 과거(I were): '마치 ~인 것처럼'. 비유적 표현으로 무중력의 초인적 능력을 묘사.
